applied_penalties: The FATCAT-material kinase hypothesis reports calibration for family node d.144.1.7/SUNID 88854 (229/229) instead of the applicable required protein-kinase-like superfamily node d.144.1/SUNID 56112 (458/458), lowering the answer by at least one point.
record.rubric_notes: The answer correctly presents five separate approximate regional hypotheses, preserves the extracellular boundary overlaps, avoids a full-chain classification, identifies extracellular support as structure-only, supplies exact model/UniProt/release provenance, reports representative SIDs and detailed FATCAT/sequence metrics, and gives strong region-specific pLDDT treatment including the mixed kinase confidence. It also clearly states that the assessment is non-official and non-definitive, treats pLDDT and FATCAT significance appropriately, includes automated-match caveats, and recognizes the one-case g.3.9 benchmark denominator. The main material defect is kinase-level calibration: the required applicable benchmark is the d.144.1 superfamily row at threshold 5 (1.0 over 458 cases), but the answer substitutes the narrower d.144.1.7 family row (1.0 over 229 cases). Relatedly, it foregrounds a d.144.1.7 family relationship more strongly than warranted even though another sequence group is d.144.1.2; the best-calibrated retained conclusion should be the d.144.1 superfamily, with d.144.1.7 only a narrower candidate. These issues prevent completeness but do not erase the otherwise extensive and appropriately caveated evidence synthesis.
